who: Peter S. Alagona, environmental historian at UC Santa Barbara, PhD in History UCLA 2006.

evidence.says: The History Department identifies Peter S. Alagona as an environmental historian and lists Tim Paulson and Brian Tyrrell among his advisees.
The authority for Alagona, Peter S. cites this UCSB faculty page and his 2006 UCLA History dissertation, Transforming conservation.

notes: Both listed students are explicitly linked to the candidate by the department.

who: Guy Alchon, historian of twentieth-century U.S. political economy at the University of Delaware, PhD Iowa 1982.

evidence.says: The 1995–1996 graduate catalogue lists Guy Alchon as an associate professor of history specializing in twentieth-century U.S. history and political economy, with a PhD from Iowa.
The authority identifies the author of The invisible hand of planning as Guy Alchon of the University of Delaware History Department, PhD University of Iowa 1982.

notes: The authority directly matches both the doctoral institution and year and the students’ university.

who: Eugene Campbell Barker, historian at the University of Texas, PhD Pennsylvania 1908.

evidence.says: The Texas State Historical Association identifies Eugene C. Barker as a University of Texas history professor from 1913 to 1951 and records his University of Pennsylvania PhD in 1908.
The authority equates Eugene C. Barker with Eugene Campbell Barker and cites A social and political history of Texas, identifying him with the University of Texas in 1932.

notes: His Texas professorship covers both dissertation years, 1934 and 1949; his doctorate matches exactly.

who: Hyman Berman, labor historian at the University of Minnesota, PhD Columbia 1956.

evidence.says: The Minnesota Historical Society records Berman’s Columbia PhD in 1956, his joining Minnesota’s History Department in 1961, his labor-history specialization, and his retirement in 2004.
The Hyman Berman authority cites a 1984 work identifying him as teaching at the University of Minnesota and a later notice identifying him as a former Minnesota history professor.

notes: The authority places him at Minnesota in 1984, one of the supplied dissertation years; the doctorate also matches.

who: John E. Woods, historian of Iran and Central Asia at the University of Chicago, PhD Princeton 1974.

evidence.says: Chicago identifies John E. Woods as professor emeritus of Iranian and Central Asian history, records Princeton University PhD 1974, and lists The Aqquyunlu among his publications.
The authority for Woods, John E. cites The Aqquyunlu and Chicago’s faculty page, identifying him as an emeritus historian of Turkey, Iran, and Central Asia.

notes: Institution, Princeton doctorate and subject match. The LC record identifies the Chicago historian among the many Woods candidates; individual student links were not independently verified.

who: Alfred S. Bradford, John Saxon Chair of Ancient History at the University of Oklahoma, PhD in History Chicago.

evidence.says: Oklahoma identifies Alfred Bradford as John Saxon Chair of Ancient History, with a History PhD from Chicago and research interests in ancient Greek and Roman history.
The Alfred S. Bradford authority cites the publisher page for The Blood-Drenched Sea, identifying its author as John Saxon Chair of Ancient History at Oklahoma.

notes: The named chair, institution, field and Chicago doctorate establish the match. The Missouri 1990 student connection was not independently verified.

who: Lamar M. Hill, historian of Tudor and Stuart Britain at UC Irvine, doctoral training at the University of London.

evidence.says: The UC memorial identifies Lamar Hill as a UC Irvine history professor who joined in 1968, studied at the University of London, supervised dissertations, and wrote Bench and Bureaucracy.
The authority equates L. M. Hill with Lamar M. Hill, identifies him as an associate professor at UC Irvine, and cites Bench and bureaucracy.
Nicole LaBouff’s museum-hosted CV records her UC Irvine History PhD studies in 2005–2013 and a Tudor England course with Lamar Hill in fall 2006.

notes: The authority and UC memorial connect the abbreviated candidate name to the same historian and works. LaBouff’s CV confirms contact during her doctorate, though it does not establish the advisor role.

who: Kristin M. Szylvian, public and urban historian formerly at Western Michigan University, History PhD Carnegie Mellon 1988.

evidence.says: Her institutional CV records a History appointment at Western Michigan beginning in August 1996 and continuing through the listed students’ 2008 and 2010 dissertation years, and a History PhD from Carnegie Mellon in December 1988.
The authority for Kristin M. Szylvian cites From tenements to the Taylor homes, identifying her as associate professor of history at Western Michigan University.

notes: The candidate’s institutional CV and authority agree with the students’ university, period and the supplied doctoral institution.
